context: Append-only row writes with an atomic finalize artifact, a sweep-process-only SIGTERM shim, and a cancellation lifecycle event; report/gate treat unfinalized runs as failed, never green.
description:
2026-07-21 adversarial UAT review finding (P2): cells.jsonl and the accounting sidecar are written only after the whole execute phase returns (tests/uat/orchestrator.py:272-280) and uat_gate_summary.json only at the very end (:504-518); only DiskFloorAbort is artifact-safe mid-sweep (:229-271). An uncaught exception or SIGKILL mid-execute loses every completed cell's durable record (raw logs survive but are unreportable via make uat-report). SIGTERM is worse: no signal handler exists anywhere in tests/uat (timeouts.py only manages the CELL subprocess group), so Python's default SIGTERM action skips the finally teardown at tests/uat/phases/execute.py:300-313 entirely - a plain `kill <pid>` leaves the Docker stack up AND loses the records, while Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt) tears down correctly. docker_cleanup.py:3-8 names hard-kill recovery as make uat-docker-cleanup's job, so the stack half is acknowledged-by-design - but kill-vs-Ctrl-C asymmetry is a footgun during multi-hour release-gate sweeps, and the durability half has no mitigation at all.

Work: append each cell's row incrementally (or flush per platform) with an explicit finalize marker so a partial file can never read as a complete sweep; SIGTERM->raise shim in the sweep process so kill == Ctrl-C; record sweep-level cancellation as a lifecycle event (today it is only inferable from a missing gate summary). Interacts with uat-evidence-provenance-binding: the finalize marker is also what the digest/gate side should require - coordinate row/marker shape, and land this SECOND if both are in flight.

anti_patterns.dont: buffer rows in memory and flush on a timer
anti_patterns.why: the failure mode being fixed is process death; timers lose the tail

anti_patterns.dont: install signal handlers inside cell subprocesses
anti_patterns.why: timeouts.py owns process-group kill semantics for cells; competing handlers break the 124/timeout contract

anti_patterns.dont: let a partial cells.jsonl pass for a complete sweep
anti_patterns.instead: explicit finalize marker; report/gate-check require it
anti_patterns.why: gate soundness: a killed sweep must stay distinguishable and non-green, or durability becomes a forgery vector

preserves.behavior: DiskFloorAbort behavior and exit codes unchanged; sweep exit codes unchanged.
cells.jsonl ROW schema unchanged (report/gate consumers parse it); the finalize marker is a separate artifact or trailing sentinel, decided with the provenance item.
timeouts.py cell-subprocess process-group kill semantics untouched.

prior_art.concept: DiskFloorAbort - the one existing artifact-safe mid-sweep abort path to generalize

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/uat -k 'sigterm or durab or incremental or finalize' -q
verifications.description: Kill mid-sweep keeps rows, tears down, exits nonzero
verifications.expected: completed cells' rows present after simulated SIGTERM; teardown invoked; unfinalized run rejected as green by report

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/uat/test_runner.py tests/uat/test_report.py tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py -q

work_units.evidence: cells_io.CellStreamWriter appends+fsyncs each row at cell completion (hooked via orchestrator _build_disk_floor_runner cell_stream); write_cells_jsonl writes the atomic .finalized marker last + clears .inprogress; make uat-report treats a lingering .inprogress w/o .finalized as INCOMPLETE (exit 2) while marker-less legacy artifacts stay green. Tests: test_sweep_durability.py w1 cases + full tests/uat lane 569 passed.
work_units.summary: Incremental per-cell append of cells.jsonl + sidecar flush (atomic finalize marker on completion); report refuses to treat an unfinalized run as green

work_units.evidence: orchestrator._install_sweep_sigterm_shim installs a sweep-process-only SIGTERM->SweepCancelled(KeyboardInterrupt) shim; run_sweep restores the prior handler in a finally; interrupt unwinds through run_execute per-platform finally (docker teardown) and exits nonzero. Tests: test_sigterm_shim_raises_sweepcancelled..., test_run_sweep_restores_previous_sigterm_handler, test_interrupt_mid_cell_still_tears_down_docker_stack.
work_units.summary: SIGTERM->raise shim in the sweep process (not cell subprocesses) so finally-teardown and nonzero exit behave exactly like Ctrl-C

work_units.evidence: SIGTERM handler records '[cancel] signal=<name> phase=<phase> ...' to uat_lifecycle.log (offset-aware timestamp via append_lifecycle_log) before raising. Test: test_sigterm_shim_raises_sweepcancelled_and_records_cancellation asserts the [cancel] line + signal name + phase.
work_units.summary: Record sweep-level cancellation (signal name, phase, timestamp) in uat_lifecycle.log
